strategies.name: Naive 8-stage all-reduce baseline
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with interleaved local bidiagonal coupling and inverse operations, exactly as shown in the seed library. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces. Represents the straightforward reference with no structural optimization—maximum dispatch overhead but simplest correctness verification.

strategies.name: Fused local-op batched all-reduce
strategies.desc: Precomputes all 8 bidiagonal coupling transformations locally as separate buffers, then dispatches all 8 all-reduces back-to-back to enable potential hardware pipelining and amortize launch overhead. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces. Trades increased local memory footprint (8× buffer copies) for better collective dispatch batching and potential overlap.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction tree
strategies.desc: Exploits the 224 = 32×7 or 28×8 factorization to perform intra-node reductions first (using device-local collectives or NCCL node-groups), then inter-node reductions. Dispatch count: 16 collectives (8 stages × 2 levels). Reduces cross-node bandwidth pressure by factor of nodes, trading doubled dispatch count for smaller effective world size per collective.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter plus all-gather composition
strategies.desc: Replaces each all-reduce with reduce-scatter (224 ranks → each gets S=1024 elements) followed by bidiagonal coupling on local shard, then all-gather to reconstruct full vector. Dispatch count: 16 collectives (8 stages × 2 primitives). Reduces per-rank communication volume from O(W·S) to O(S) per stage but doubles primitive count.

strategies.name: Algebraic loop fusion with single final all-reduce
strategies.desc:
Analytically composes the 8 forward bidiagonal couplings and 7 inverse operations into a single equivalent linear transformation matrix (or recursive formula), applies it locally to input x, then performs one all-reduce at the end. Dispatch count: 1 all-reduce. Maximizes local compute (O(W²) operations per rank) to eliminate 7 collective dispatches—optimal for high-latency, high-throughput networks.
